description: Computational prior registry for matrix accessibility, retention, and process-state behavior. These priors are the cheap-first calibration layer used before any expensive QM refinement.

accessibility_windows.source: Asen 2022 DSC/DTNB + Li 2025 Ellman SH envelope, retained as a conservative pea-isolate interpolation while exact benchmark-condition values remain unmeasured
accessibility_windows.notes: Directly informed by validated pea process-state anchors, but still transferred to the benchmark condition rather than measured there.

accessibility_windows.source: Foods 11(21):3505 soy free-SH anchor for native versus 70 C SPI plus repo synthesis from Kutzli 2020 / Naik 2021 on glycinin and beta-conglycinin burial
accessibility_windows.notes: Soy isolate accessibility is now tied to a direct SPI Ellman anchor, while exact benchmark-condition transfer still remains unresolved.

accessibility_windows.source: Bounded mycoprotein accessibility prior from fungal cell-wall entrapment and heat-softening literature synthesis retained as a directional planning prior
accessibility_windows.notes: Mycoprotein is now a first-class matrix family with explicit bounded priors, but the window remains directional until direct free-SH / free-amino anchors are encoded.

denaturation_heuristics.source: Asen 2022 DSC/DTNB thermal window + Li 2025 free-SH response; calibrated so pea isolate stays mostly native at 40C but opens progressively by 90-140C
denaturation_heuristics.notes: This is a low-cost interpolation heuristic derived from pea literature anchors, not a direct benchmark fit.

denaturation_heuristics.source: Pea concentrate inherits the Asen 2022 / Li 2025 pea thermal envelope with a modest fiber-burial penalty
denaturation_heuristics.notes: Concentrate values remain transferred from isolate-scale anchors with an explicit burial penalty.

denaturation_heuristics.source: Foods 11(21):3505 free-SH increase at 70 C plus soy globulin burial synthesis from Kutzli 2020 / Naik 2021
denaturation_heuristics.notes: Soy process-state realism now includes a direct SPI free-SH anchor, but exact benchmark-condition denaturation still remains transferred rather than measured.

denaturation_heuristics.source: Soy concentrate inherits the soy-isolate thermal envelope with added concentrate burial
denaturation_heuristics.notes: Concentrate state is an explicit prior, not a measured calibration.

denaturation_heuristics.source: Bounded mycoprotein thermal-opening prior derived from fungal-protein heat-softening literature synthesis
denaturation_heuristics.notes: Directional mycoprotein process-state prior only; use for planning and trust reporting rather than quantitative closure.

volatile_class_profiles.source: Conservative class-aware trapping overlay: aldehydes bind most strongly, sulfur volatiles and alcohols escape somewhat more readily
volatile_class_profiles.notes: Used as a class-level surrogate until compound-specific matrix retention data exists for meaty sulfur targets.

volatile_class_profiles.source: Pea concentrate inherits stronger aldehyde/furan trapping from the pea family plus a concentrate penalty
volatile_class_profiles.notes: Concentrate trapping remains a structured prior.

volatile_class_profiles.source: Conservative soy overlay: aldehydes still bind more strongly than sulfur/alcohol classes, but less severely than pea
volatile_class_profiles.notes: Useful for relative ranking, not for direct quantitative release claims.

volatile_class_profiles.source: Soy concentrate inherits the soy family overlay with added burial
Bounded mycoprotein class overlay retained as a literature-bounded directional surrogate
volatile_class_profiles.notes: Use for directional matrix-family comparisons until direct mycoprotein release data is encoded.

matrix_corrections.source: Asen 2022 DSC/DTNB + Li 2025 Ellman SH envelope; values remain a conservative PPI interpolation because the exact 95C pH 5.5 benchmark condition still lacks direct wet-lab measurement
matrix_corrections.notes: This is a reliability improvement over a generic heuristic because the numbers now explicitly track the validated pea process-state literature.

matrix_corrections.source: Pea-isolate accessibility envelope with added fiber burial penalty
matrix_corrections.notes: Concentrate values remain transferred from isolate anchors.

matrix_corrections.source: Soy isolate envelope anchored to Foods 11(21):3505 free-SH shift plus repo literature on glycinin and beta-conglycinin burial and accessibility transfer
matrix_corrections.notes: Still a transferred correction rather than a direct benchmark-condition fit, but no longer a pure repo-only synthesis.

matrix_corrections.source: Soy concentrate envelope derived from soy-isolate globulin burial (glycinin/beta-conglycinin) with added fiber/concentrate penalty; repo anchors: Kutzli 2020 / Naik 2021 synthesis plus soy-polysaccharide conjugation trapping notes in docs/Maillard_Plant_based.md
matrix_corrections.notes: Explicit prior rather than direct calibration.

matrix_corrections.source: Bounded mycoprotein correction prior from fungal-matrix accessibility and release literature synthesis
matrix_corrections.notes: Directional mycoprotein prior only; intended for bounded ranking support and trust reporting rather than quantitative closure.

pyrazine_control_priors.notes: Directional pyrazine control surface: pH dominates, fructose and pentoses increase pyrazines, peptide-rich systems can intensify pyrazine formation.

strecker_crosstalk_priors.source: Lincoln et al. (2025), Sustainable Food Proteins 10.1002/sfp2.1044
strecker_crosstalk_priors.summary: Glucose plus lipid plus polyphenol systems in SPI/PPI can suppress Strecker aldehydes through alpha-dicarbonyl competition while altering post-heating oxidative stability.
strecker_crosstalk_priors.notes: Directional prior only; full quantitative volatile units and internal-standard details remain unresolved in the repo.

furanone_priors.source: Blank and Fay 1996 plus Watanabe 2015 meat-side reference context
furanone_priors.notes: Mechanistic expectation only: pentose plus alanine supports HEMF; pentose plus glycine or alanine supports DMHF.
Bounded bridge prior tying caramel/furanone intermediates to sulfur-positive branches. Use for Family 09 reporting and routing support without claiming one-condition endpoint closure.

furanone_priors.source: Brands & van Boekel (2002) with bounded absolute-yield context carried forward from the repo's Hauck & Tressl 1999 HDMF synthesis cross-reference
furanone_priors.notes: Bounded Family 09 support prior showing that HDMF can arise directly from methylglyoxal-rich fragmentation chemistry without an amino-acid partner. Use for runtime-visible C3-route context only; do not treat this as a full standalone caramelization closure model.

thiamine_pathway_priors.source: Cerny 2007 isotope-labeled thiamine partitioning plus Cerny & Guntz-Dubini 2008 pH-resolved MFT yields and Hofmann et al. 1996 beef-realistic synergy context
thiamine_pathway_priors.notes: Use for bounded Family 03 support scoring: Cerny 2007 sets mixed-source attribution, Cerny 2008 sets the pH-sensitive MFT window, Hofmann 1996 sets a conservative mixed-system synergy floor plus a dilute mixed-system uplift ceiling for low-total-precursor cases, and De Leyn 2019 attenuates pre-extrusion thiamine survival.

Primary aqueous Arrhenius anchor for Family 03. Use to keep acidic thiamine systems slow, neutral systems fast, and neutral high-concentration systems explicitly super-linear instead of treating thiamine disappearance as a single global first-order constant.

Bounded Family 03 aw-dependent Arrhenius support prior for starch-like matrices. Use to attenuate thiamine survival under wetter extrusion-like conditions and modestly relax that penalty under drier low-moisture conditions without replacing the Cerny yield surface or the Voelker aqueous pH anchor.

Bounded metal-catalysis correction for Family 03. Use to accelerate thiamine loss when iron-rich or copper-rich plant matrices are present, with Fe3+ as the strongest practical catalyst in the curated literature surface.

nucleotide_pathway_priors.source: Matoba, Terao & Fujimaki 1988 IMP/GMP hydrolysis kinetics plus Mouritsen 2024 threshold-fold data, Yamaguchi & Ninomiya 2000 EUC constants, and Nakamura 1988 ribose-liberation context
nucleotide_pathway_priors.notes: Use for bounded Family 04 support scoring: preserve IMP/GMP as upstream umami support at mild thermal load, then shift part of that support toward ribose delivery as hydrolysis accelerates under extrusion-like severity.
Directional donor-potency prior for upstream sugar routing. Use to keep ribose and especially R5P clearly above glucose when prioritizing sulfur-positive routes.
Bounded donor-priority prior that ties stronger sulfur output from ribose and G6P to the same literature context that reported nucleotide-pool relevance in cooked meat systems.
Bounded phosphorylated-sugar prior for HDMF-rich routing. Use to keep G6P above glucose when furanone-support signals matter, without claiming endpoint closure in plant matrices.
Low-temperature EUC window anchor for Family 04. Use for scientist-facing mild-heating context and bounded PBMA transfer reasoning, not as a universal kinetic override for nucleotide hydrolysis.

Ingredient-source reference window for Family 04. Use to expose how strongly yeast-extract grade and AMP-deaminase treatment can change practical nucleotide support without replacing the existing Matoba or Soladoye thermal logic.

Ingredient-source reference window for Family 04. Use to expose species-specific mushroom GMP and EUC context when clean-label nucleotide support is supplied by shiitake, porcini, enoki, or oyster powders.

carbonyl_donor_priors.notes: Quantitative donor-hierarchy prior for Family 07. Use to keep pentoses and especially ribose clearly above glucose/fructose while preserving the strong disaccharide penalty, without claiming matrix-specific endpoint closure in plant proteins.

Bounded rhamnose-plus-proline HDMF prior for Family 07. Use to expose that rhamnose can drive unusually strong HDMF support when proline is present, without reclassifying rhamnose as a universal fast donor across plant matrices.

sulfur_peptide_priors.source: Bounded sulfur-support prior distilled from Wang et al. GSH vs cysteine sulfur yields, Xu et al. peptide hierarchy, and Nishimura & Abe soy hydrolysate intake support
sulfur_peptide_priors.notes: Use for Family 05 runtime scoring as a bounded uplift prior. It supports sulfur-positive interpretation, not absolute MFT or FFT concentration claims in SPI benchmarks.

Bounded Family 05 kokumi prior for CaSR-active glutathione and gamma-glutamyl peptides. Use to expose mouthfulness support alongside sulfur-positive interpretation without claiming full sensory closure in plant matrices.
High-OAV sulfur-support prior for pentose plus sulfur model systems. Use as bounded evidence that MFT and FFT remain strongly favored when sulfur donors are paired with xylose and glutamate support.

retention_binding_priors.notes: Bounded retention prior from protein-aroma binding literature. Use to support Family 11 retention reasoning without pretending compound-specific benchmark closure.
Directional binding prior for protein-aroma interaction hierarchy. Use for bounded headspace-recovery interpretation, not absolute calibration.

Directional PPI sulfur-volatile binding prior for Family 11. Use to keep sulfur retention non-neutral in pea systems and to interpolate initial non-covalent binding posture before higher-temperature trapping pathways dominate.

Bounded beta-cyclodextrin encapsulation prior for Family 08 guardrails. Use as a partial aldehyde-suppression surface for hexanal, nonanal, and unsaturated aldehydes, not as a complete off-note elimination model.

dicarbonyl_sink_priors.notes: Bounded soy-isoflavone prior for AGE and dicarbonyl suppression. Use as a guardrail-side modifier with explicit uncertainty, not as endpoint closure.

polyphenol_thiol_capping_priors.notes: Bounded polyphenol-thiol capping prior for Family 13. Use to reduce free-thiol availability when strong catechol-type capping cues are active, without claiming endpoint closure.

lipid_offnote_priors.notes: Bounded lipid off-note prior for highly unsaturated systems. Use as a guardrail for arachidonic-acid-rich oxidative branches and reporting, not as a concentration closure claim.
Bounded off-note prior for oxidized-lipid systems where 4-HNE can route into pyrrolic aroma defects. Use as a reporting and guardrail prior, not as endpoint concentration closure.

Bounded sulfur-quench prior for Family 02. Use to penalize MFT expectations when lipid-derived aldehydes rise into the competitive regime instead of treating sulfur yield as independent from off-note burden.
Directional lipid-off-note prior for Family 02. Use to weight unsaturated aldehyde branches above saturated analogues in guardrail and crosstalk reporting without claiming a full kinetic mechanism.

dicarbonyl_fragmentation_priors.notes: Deterministic 3-DG retro-aldol branching prior for AGE and diketone reasoning. Use as a bounded routing prior rather than a full kinetic mechanism.

ascorbic_pathway_priors.notes: Primary Family 14 Arrhenius anchor for extrusion-like AA degradation. Use to keep ascorbic-acid dicarbonyl release explicitly pH-sensitive instead of treating AA as a fixed generic precursor source.
Family 14 cross-link hierarchy prior for AA-derived dicarbonyl trapping. Use to preserve Lys > Arg > His routing in safety-facing AGE reasoning rather than relying on Ea alone.

Family 14 pentosidine-equivalence prior for AA-driven cross-link burden. Use to keep antioxidant ascorbate additions visible as a bounded AGE source term instead of treating AA as chemically benign once dicarbonyl formation starts.

melanoidin_trapping_priors.notes: Family 16 trapping prior for CROSSPY-driven thioether adduction. Use to justify non-recoverable MFT loss when melanoidin burden is already high, rather than treating thiol suppression as purely reversible binding.

Compact Family 16 architecture prior for Maillard-conjugated pea hydrolysate systems. Use to surface polymer-growth and trapping-risk direction when gum arabic and hydrolysate cues are present, not as a universal rheology solver.

dft_kinetic_priors.description: Per-reaction kinetic priors for the priority computational-gap DFT targets (families 11-16). Current tier is the best available estimate; target tier is selective_dft_anchor after wB97M-V//r2SCAN-3c completes. Run scripts/run_computational_gap_dft.py, then scripts/generators/ingest_computational_gap_dft_results.py, then scripts/generators/promote_computational_gap_dft_results.py to promote completed non-fast entries.

entries.honest_label: Selective DFT anchor, ranking support only until matrix benchmark closure
entries.promotion_note: Promoted from completed computational-gap DFT execution; benchmark closure remains gated by matrix observables.

HCW Family 14 surrogate for an upstream ascorbic-acid dicarbonyl source, DFT validation pending, ±factor 2-5; bounded calibration
entries.computational_method: Family 14 HCW literature surrogate (bounded upstream dicarbonyl source)
entries.surrogate_reaction: Dehydroascorbic-acid ring opening and hydration are treated as a bounded upstream source of reactive dicarbonyl pressure rather than as a validated elementary xTB endpoint.
entries.surrogate_assumption: The Family 14 runtime lane stays anchored to the HCW effective barrier until a balanced dehydroascorbic-acid ring-opening pair is regenerated for xTB/DFT.
